limitations: Company model benchmarks are not identical to tests of the deployed ChatGPT configuration.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: ChatGPT cannot reliably use factual information like Wikipedia's and has no explicit, stable internal world model.

statement.excerpt: But ChatGPT can’t leverage that kind of information reliably, and doesn’t have its own an explicit, stable, internal model.
statement.document_title: Generative AI’s crippling and widespread failure to induce robust models of the world

from_speaker: can’t leverage that kind of information reliably
doesn’t have its own an explicit, stable, internal model
our_interpretation: The claim joins two propositions: unreliable use of well-documented facts and absence of an explicit, stable internal world model.
Reliability means dependable factual answers across ordinary contexts, not perfect accuracy on every possible question.
A behavioral error does not establish the absence of an internal representation.
No version or period is named. I use June 2025 through publication as the latest monthly observation window; older model evaluations remain context.
The Harry Shearer example motivates the claim but is not treated as an independently verified experiment.
criteria.support_condition: Replicated tests of the relevant ChatGPT configuration show material factual inconsistency, and independent architectural or mechanistic evidence establishes the claimed absence of an explicit, stable model.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Matched tests establish dependable use of the relevant facts under ordinary contextual variation, or mechanistic evidence identifies a stable, explicit, updatable internal model in the relevant ChatGPT system.

evidence.explanation: SimpleQA documents factual errors and examines consistency over repeated answers. It is deliberately challenging and does not establish June 2025 ChatGPT reliability on ordinary Wikipedia facts or the absence of an internal model.

The report records factual errors on questions about people and differences among models. It supports concern about factual reliability, but neither identifies Marcus's ChatGPT configuration nor tests the asserted absence of a stable internal model.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Reproducible tests of an identified June 2025 ChatGPT configuration across factual prompts and contexts, together with direct evidence about its internal representations and updating mechanisms.
